primitives.name: Temporal Identity Rotation
primitives.verbatim_quote: I said I wanted a sideline reporter > that looked like a SFW [tasteful] one week, cheerleader the next, sideline > report next and halftime report the following.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'W': 'dimensionless week index', 'L(W)': 'look type at time W', 'F(W)': 'format type at time W'}
primitives.assumptions: Presenter identity is a periodic function of time with fixed cycle length; look and format are mutually exclusive per week.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When W exceeds cycle length, L(W) and F(W) repeat with phase shift.

layer2.mapping: The weekly rotation maps to a cyclic group Z_n where n is the number of distinct looks/formats.
layer2.telemetry: Weekly look/format compliance score from operator review.

primitives.name: Synthetic Presenter Quality Bound
primitives.verbatim_quote: Honesty boundary (non-negotiable) The presenter reads as real *production quality* — writing, pacing, and looks good enough that nobody thinks "cheap AI clip." It does **not** deceive: the small "Synthetic presenter" disclosure chip stays on synthetic video surfaces.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Q_{presenter}': 'quality metric of presenter output', 'D_{disclosure}': 'visibility of synthetic disclosure flag'}
primitives.assumptions: Quality threshold Q_{presenter} must exceed a minimum acceptable value; disclosure D_{disclosure} must remain visible.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If Q_{presenter} < threshold or D_{disclosure} = 0, synthetic output is flagged for review.

layer2.mapping: Quality bound ensures synthetic output meets production standards without deceptive intent, aligning with GSI's ethical inference framework.
layer2.telemetry: Automated content-safety scan results and human review scores.

primitives.name: Scripted Data Alignment
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Script** — drafted from real graded data only (board state, Beat rows, transmission segments).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S(t)': 'script content at time t', 'D_{real}(t)': 'real-time data input at time t'}
primitives.assumptions: Script generation is deterministic and data-driven; S(t) is a function of D_{real}(t).
primitives.breakdown_regime: If D_{real}(t) is absent or corrupted, S(t) defaults to static template.

layer2.mapping: Script alignment mirrors a feedback control loop where real-time data drives narrative structure.
layer2.telemetry: Data integrity score and script deviation from real-time inputs.

Failure modes include loss of data integrity, breach of quality bounds, or misalignment of identity rotation.
